recipe: Avoid calling non-idempotent functions like `new Date()` or `Math.random()` during render; instead, move them into a `useEffect` or an event handler.
trigger_condition: You need to use a function whose output changes on every call (e.g., `new Date()`, `Math.random()`) inside a component or hook body.
evidence: This doesn't mean you shouldn't use non-idempotent functions like `new Date()` _at all_ – you should just avoid using them [during render](#how-does-react-run-your-code).
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: You may freely create and mutate local variables (e.g., an array) during render, as long as the variable is re-created on every render and not shared outside the component.
trigger_condition: You are building a list or collection of elements inside a component's render body and are unsure whether mutating a local array is acceptable.
evidence: In general, while mutation is not idiomatic in React, _local_ mutation is absolutely fine:
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Never mutate a value that was created outside the current render scope (e.g., a module-level or closure variable); create it fresh inside render each time.
trigger_condition: You are pushing to or reassigning a variable that persists across multiple renders of the same component.
evidence: Components and Hooks should [never modify values that aren't created locally](#mutation) in render.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Calling a one-time lazy-initialization function (e.g., `SuperCalculator.initializeIfNotReady()`) during render is acceptable as long as it does not affect the rendering of other components.
trigger_condition: You need to ensure an external library or module is initialized before using it, and you want to do it at component render time.
evidence: Lazy initialization is also fine despite not being fully "pure":
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Do not directly modify the DOM (e.g., `document.title = ...`) inside a component's render logic; use an Effect to synchronize with the DOM instead.
trigger_condition: You want to update a DOM property or attribute (like `document.title`) as part of rendering a component.
evidence: Side effects that are directly visible to the user are not allowed in the render logic of React components.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: If a piece of code is written at the top level of a component or hook function body, assume it runs during render and treat it as render-phase code (keep it pure and idempotent).
trigger_condition: You are unsure whether a line of code in your component or hook executes during render or only on user interaction.
evidence: if it's written at the top level like in the example below, there's a good chance it runs during render.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Never mutate a prop object directly; instead create a new value (e.g., a copy) and use that in your component logic.
trigger_condition: You need to modify a value that was passed into your component as a prop.
evidence: Props are immutable because if you mutate them, the application will produce inconsistent output, which can be hard to debug as it may or may not work depending on the circumstances.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Never mutate a value passed as an argument to a hook; make a copy (e.g., via spread) before modifying it, since the hook may memoize based on the original reference.
trigger_condition: You need to modify a value that you are passing into a custom or built-in hook.
evidence: Once values are passed to a hook, you should not modify them. Like props in JSX, values become immutable when passed to a hook.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure

recipe: Move any mutation to before the JSX expression that uses the value; never mutate a value after it has already been passed to JSX.
trigger_condition: You need to change a value that has already been used in a JSX expression earlier in the same render.
evidence: Don't mutate values after they've been used in JSX. Move the mutation to before the JSX is created.
source_name: react.dev reference: Components and Hooks must be pure
